title: Newton's apple: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Isaac Newton lived in a quiet English village.
The apple landed on a hard rock.
Isaac picked up the apple and let it go.
Gravity pulls objects away from the Earth.
The Moon crashed into the Earth.
Isaac spent many years studying and calculating.
Where was Isaac sitting when the apple fell?
items.why: “One sunny afternoon, he sat beneath an apple tree, enjoying the peaceful garden.”

items.q: What do we call the force that pulls objects toward the Earth?
What did Isaac look at that evening?
items.why: “That evening, Isaac looked up at the beautiful Moon.”

items.q: How is the Moon moving through space?
items.why: “The Moon is moving sideways through space.”

items.q: What did Isaac want to know?
items.why: “But Isaac wanted to know why they fell.”

items.after: red apple fell from the tree.

items.before: He picked up the apple and held it
That is how the Moon stays in

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Isaac Newton saw an apple fall and wondered why. He thought that an invisible force, gravity, pulls objects toward the Earth. Later, he understood that gravity also keeps the Moon in orbit around the Earth.

items.q: What questions did Isaac ask when the apple fell?
items.model: "Why did the apple fall down? Why didn't it fly up into the sky?"

items.q: Why doesn't the Moon crash into the Earth?
items.model: The Moon is moving sideways through space while gravity pulls it inward. It keeps falling toward the Earth, but keeps missing it.

items.q: What does the same force help explain?
items.model: It helps explain the movements of planets and their moons.

items.q: What is a question about the world that you would like to answer?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: Isaac sat beneath an apple tree
A ripe red apple fell on the grass
Isaac held the apple high and let it go
Isaac looked at the Moon that evening
Isaac spent many years studying and calculating
